nonBlockingIssues.description: ~300 lines of dead legacy _monitor_* methods with powershell/wmic subprocess calls remain in behavioral_monitor.py (lines 468-773). These are unreachable from the new Docker-based code path but add unnecessary dead code.
Docker sandbox timeout is silently capped at 30 seconds without logging when caller passes a larger value.
analysis_depth parameter is read from args but not declared in MCP tool input_schema, so callers cannot discover or set it.
Catches bare TimeoutError instead of explicit asyncio.TimeoutError — functionally correct in Python 3.14 but slightly less clear.
Uses deprecated datetime.utcnow() (deprecated since Python 3.12) while the same commit's memory_forensics.py uses the preferred datetime.now(timezone.utc).
Uses str | None union syntax requiring Python 3.10+ runtime (mitigated by __future__ annotations import).

suggestedGuidanceUpdates.suggestion: Add convention: when replacing an implementation (e.g., Docker sandbox replacing powershell host monitoring), workers should remove the dead legacy code rather than leaving ~300 lines of unreachable methods. This prevents accumulation of security-sensitive dead code (subprocess calls to powershell, wmic).
suggestedGuidanceUpdates.evidence: docker-sandbox worker left 8 dead _monitor_* methods (lines 468-773) with subprocess.run(['powershell'...]) calls in behavioral_monitor.py. Confirmed zero callers via codebase grep.

suggestedGuidanceUpdates.suggestion: Add convention: prefer datetime.now(timezone.utc) over deprecated datetime.utcnow() (deprecated since Python 3.12, PEP 670). This prevents inconsistencies within the same module.
suggestedGuidanceUpdates.evidence: volatility3-memory worker used utcnow() in volatility_analyzer.py while the same commit's memory_forensics.py uses the correct datetime.now(timezone.utc).
